To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the residues involved in FecR binding are located on one side of FecA's signaling domain, and that FecA's iron binding and transport domains are influenced by the signaling domain.
FecA mutations that reduce FecR interaction and transcriptional activity are localized on one side in the FecA structure and that the mutations affect the structure of the transport domain.
residues involved in FecR binding are localized on one side on the FecA signal domain and that the signal domain is also involved in the structure of the transporter domain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new model for the interaction of two proteins involved in signal transduction.
the interaction of the FecR protein with the periplasmic domain of FecA.
the identification of the FecR binding sites and with a possible role of the Fec signaling domain in the structure of the transporter domain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FecA-FecR interaction is a prerequisite for iron uptake, and that FecR binding to FecA induces the transport function.
the FecR-FecA interaction involves residues on one side of FecA, which is the same side where the ferric cit rate binding sites are located.
the FecA/FecR interaction site is localized on one side, and that mutations in the interaction site affect the structure of the transporter domain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the FecA-FecR complex is a dynamic structure that can be stabilized in a functional conformation by the binding of ferric citrate.
the FecR-FecA interaction involves the FecA C terminus and that the interaction is important for the FecA function as an iron transport protein.
the interaction with FecA is important for the function of the FecR signaling protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the FecR-binding site on FecA is located on one side of its signaling domain.
FecA is a modular protein with a signaling domain that is distinct from the transporter domain.
the FecA/FecR interaction is localized on one side, which might allow for the formation of a signaling domain/transporter domain interface that is not disrupted by the FecR binding.
